facility_roles.note: First document read that places SPICE in the proposed TESSERACT experiment at LSM (Nucl. Phys. B, received 9 January 2024); the TAUP 2025 slides repeat it ('Commissioning at Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane'). SPICE is otherwise an R&D programme at US institutions.
facility_roles.quote: Combined with the US-based SPICE and HeRALD technologies, the TESSERACT at LSM experiment will then allow to probe DM candidates over 12 orders of magnitude in mass

intervals.label: SPICE/HeRALD R&D; proposed for LSM as a TESSERACT module
intervals.note: Earliest dated paper read carrying the combined collaboration tag; the proposal to host SPICE at LSM dates from 2022 (Nucl. Phys. B 2024). SPICE itself has no separately dated founding in the sources read.

intervals.label: planned installation of the TESSERACT setups (including SPICE) at LSM
intervals.quote: The two setups will be in LSM between 2027 and 2028

quantity.quote: In our final dataset, we report a world-leading energy resolution of 258.5$\pm$0.4 meV in the 1 mm thick detector.

lineage.quote: The SPICE portion of the TESSERACT program uses substrates with strong optical phonon modes

Separate from experiment:tesseract because the collaboration's own site calls SPICE and HeRALD 'two experiments' and a Comm. Phys. 2026 review writes 'the SPICE experiment'; the Nucl. Phys. B paper calls them detector technologies.

physics_goals.quote: The primary goal for these polar crystal detectors is to search for single optical phonons produced by electromagnetically interacting DM via scattering (3 keV ≤ 𝑚DM ≤ 1 MeV) and via absorption (100 meV ≤ 𝑚DM ≤ 1 eV).
physics_goals.value: Search for single optical phonons produced by electromagnetically interacting dark matter (scattering 3 keV to 1 MeV, absorption 100 meV to 1 eV)

summary.plain: SPICE is a dark matter detector that uses small crystals of sapphire, quartz or gallium arsenide, with superconducting sensors that feel the tiniest vibrations a dark matter particle could cause. It is part of TESSERACT and is proposed for the Modane underground laboratory.
summary.technical: Sub-eV Polar Interactions Cryogenic Experiment: 1 cm^3 Al2O3 and SiO2 polar crystals (single optical phonons from electromagnetically coupled DM: scattering 3 keV-1 MeV, absorption 100 meV-1 eV) and GaAs scintillator (inelastic electron recoils, scattering above 1 MeV, absorption above 1.5 eV), with two separately read-out athermal-phonon TES arrays per pixel to reject sensor-coupled backgrounds. A Si surface prototype set limits at 44-87 MeV/c^2 in 2025. Proposed host: LSM as a TESSERACT module.
